summary.name: Helium Browser
summary.one_liner: Helium is a free, open-source, Chromium-based desktop browser that blocks ads, trackers, and cookie banners by default and removes Google service dependencies.
use_cases: Browse the web with ads and trackers blocked by default
Jump directly to websites using !bang shortcuts instead of search results
Use Chromium extensions in a browser without Google services
Run a privacy-focused desktop browser on macOS, Windows, or Linux
summary.what_it_does: Helium is a Chromium-based desktop browser with Google service dependencies removed. It blocks ads, trackers, cookie banners and third-party cookies by default, and it adds noise to certain web APIs to make fingerprinting harder. It supports all Chromium extensions and can import them from an existing Chromium browser, and it anonymizes Chrome Web Store requests. Its !bangs feature lets users jump straight to a website from the address bar, processed locally. All components and online services are open source on GitHub, and the services can be self-hosted.
notable: Ad, tracker, and cookie banner blocking enabled by default
Open-source Chromium build with Google services removed, self-hostable services
!bangs search shortcuts processed locally, skipping search results
Anonymized Chrome Web Store requests for extension downloads and updates
caveats: No Widevine DRM support, so some streaming services may not play
No built-in password manager; a separate one must be used
No data sync yet and not on mobile; desktop only, in beta
Automatic updates on macOS and Windows require Helium services to be enabled
